# CreatePhysicsWorld 〔BlitzLLVM〕

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Physics](Blitz3D-Physics)

</div>


```blitzbasic
CreatePhysicsWorld:Int32 max_bodies:Int32=0
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_bodies` | In | Int32 | `0` | How many bodies the world can hold, 0 for 10240. Memory is reserved for them, so do not ask for far more than needed. |

**Returns:** The handle of the world.

## Description

**〔BlitzLLVM〕** This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Creates a physics world of its own and returns its handle. A world holds rigid bodies and simulates them; bodies of different worlds never touch each other, which is how effects that would need a lot of work with boolean geometry (a region that only some things collide with, a second set of rules) are done. The default world, number 0, always exists once it is used and can not be freed.

## Differences

* The original has no such command. This is an extension; programs that use it do not compile with the original Blitz3D.
